_provenance.title: National curriculum in England: geography programmes of study
_provenance.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
_provenance.scope: Statutory programme-of-study statements only (the 'Pupils should be taught' lists), verbatim. Non-statutory notes and guidance, aims, purpose of study and appendices are not included.

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: name and locate the world’s 7 continents and 5 oceans

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: name, locate and identify characteristics of the 4 countries and capital cities of the United Kingdom and its surrounding seas

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: understand geographical similarities and differences through studying the human and physical geography of a small area of the United Kingdom, and of a small area in a contrasting non-European country

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: identify seasonal and daily weather patterns in the United Kingdom and the location of hot and cold areas of the world in relation to the Equator and the North and South Poles

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: use basic geographical vocabulary to refer to:

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: key physical features, including: beach, cliff, coast, forest, hill, mountain, sea, ocean, river, soil, valley, vegetation, season and weather

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: key human features, including: city, town, village, factory, farm, house, office, port, harbour and shop

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: use world maps, atlases and globes to identify the United Kingdom and its countries, as well as the countries, continents and oceans studied at this key stage

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: use simple compass directions (north, south, east and west) and locational and directional language [for example, near and far, left and right], to describe the location of features and routes on a map

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: use aerial photographs and plan perspectives to recognise landmarks and basic human and physical features; devise a simple map; and use and construct basic symbols in a key

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: use simple fieldwork and observational skills to study the geography of their school and its grounds and the key human and physical features of its surrounding environment

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: locate the world’s countries, using maps to focus on Europe (including the location of Russia) and North and South America, concentrating on their environmental regions, key physical and human characteristics, countries, and major cities

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: name and locate counties and cities of the United Kingdom, geographical regions and their identifying human and physical characteristics, key topographical features (including hills, mountains, coasts and rivers), and land-use patterns; and understand how some of these aspects have changed over time

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: identify the position and significance of latitude, longitude, Equator, Northern Hemisphere, Southern Hemisphere, the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, Arctic and Antarctic Circle, the Prime/Greenwich Meridian and time zones (including day and night)

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: understand geographical similarities and differences through the study of human and physical geography of a region of the United Kingdom, a region in a European country, and a region in North or South America

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: describe and understand key aspects of:

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: physical geography, including: climate zones, biomes and vegetation belts, rivers, mountains, volcanoes and earthquakes, and the water cycle

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: human geography, including: types of settlement and land use, economic activity including trade links, and the distribution of natural resources including energy, food, minerals and water

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: use maps, atlases, globes and digital/computer mapping to locate countries and describe features studied

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: use the 8 points of a compass, 4- and 6-figure grid references, symbols and key (including the use of Ordnance Survey maps) to build their knowledge of the United Kingdom and the wider world

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: use fieldwork to observe, measure record and present the human and physical features in the local area using a range of methods, including sketch maps, plans and graphs, and digital technologies

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: extend their locational knowledge and deepen their spatial awareness of the world’s countries, using maps of the world to focus on Africa, Russia, Asia (including China and India), and the Middle East, focusing on their environmental regions, including polar and hot deserts, key physical and human characteristics, countries and major cities

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: understand geographical similarities, differences and links between places through the study of the human and physical geography of a region in Africa and a region in Asia

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: understand, through the use of detailed place-based exemplars at a variety of scales, the key processes in:

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: physical geography relating to: geological timescales and plate tectonics; rocks, weathering and soils; weather and climate, including the change in climate from the Ice Age to the present; and glaciation, hydrology and coasts

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: human geography relating to: population and urbanisation; international development; economic activity in the primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary sectors; and the use of natural resources

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: understand how human and physical processes interact to influence and change landscapes, environments and the climate; and how human activity relies on the effective functioning of natural systems

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: build on their knowledge of globes, maps and atlases, and apply and develop this knowledge routinely in the classroom and in the field

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: interpret Ordnance Survey maps in the classroom and the field, including using grid references and scale, topographical and other thematic mapping, and aerial and satellite photographs

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: use Geographical Information Systems (GIS) to view, analyse and interpret places and data

statements.subject: geography
statements.text: use fieldwork in contrasting locations to collect, analyse and draw conclusions from geographical data, using multiple sources of increasingly complex information
